solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spatter liquid as worker in pub

indicators.note: Liquid things flow and lose their shape, so the letters run into a new order.

explanation.surface: A careless drinker slops beer over the barman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid' looks like the thing being spattered, but it is the instruction to rearrange SPATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster is one who draws beer from the tap in an inn or pub.

clue.text: Bird in rush, changing direction at last

indicators.note: The last letter is a direction.

explanation.surface: A bird darts into a clump of rushes and veers off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' suggests the reed a bird would hide in; here it is the verb, TEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater duck.

clue.text: Empty talk from chum, mean not disclosing age?

explanation.surface: A friend who is cagey about their age and does a lot of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' is the noun, an average; take AGE out and AVER is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver is lengthy, idle chatter.

clue.text: What can dry up closed water source abruptly

parts.note: a door pulled to is closed

indicators.note: abruptly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A spring that has been sealed off and suddenly runs dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closed' gives TO, as in a door pushed to.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is the cloth used for drying off the body or the washing-up.

clue.text: Fanatical state's dispatch ceding power to bishop

indicators.note: ceding means giving up the power letter from the speed word
to says which letter takes the place of the one ceded

parts.note: to do something with dispatch is to do it with speed, or rapidity
P is the physics symbol for power
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A church power struggle in which authority passes to a bishop with indecent speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the P in RAPIDITY for B.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabidity is extreme zeal or fury, the condition of a rabid fanatic.

clue.text: Woman is arch, beginning to tease

indicators.note: The beginning of 'tease' is its first letter.

explanation.surface: A woman described as arch and playfully teasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch' reads as the adjective, mischievous, which suits a tease; it is the noun, a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain first-name definition: 'woman' stands for any woman's name, and Bridget is one.

clue.text: Runs into wood for gun's component

explanation.surface: Someone flees into the woods to fetch part of a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like a verb of flight; it is the R of a cricket scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: The breech is the rear part of a gun barrel where it is loaded.

clue.text: This writer's demonstrating on the right path?

parts.note: this writer = I; this writer's = I'M

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be showing they are on the right track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter, so I; with the 's read as 'is' it becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone improving is getting better, heading the right way.

clue.text: Bats eating tip of native plant

indicators.note: Bats means crazy, so the letters go haywire.
The tip of a word is its first letter.

explanation.surface: Bats feeding on the flower of a local plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating' looks like a container instruction around N; it is fodder, rearranged along with N.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentian is a mountain plant with deep blue flowers.

clue.text: Stealing unusual rug in store

indicators.note: Unusual: the letters are put in an unusual order.

explanation.surface: A shoplifter pockets an odd rug on display in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In store' looks like a container; the whole phrase RUG IN STORE is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousering money is British slang for pocketing it, often dishonestly.

clue.text: Permitted female to leave uncultivated expert

indicators.note: the female letter is made to leave, dropping out of the word

explanation.surface: A woman is allowed to quit her job as a skilled hand on untilled land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncultivated' looks like part of the picture of farm work, but it supplies the word the female letter leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Something allowable is acceptable under the rules, so it is permitted.

clue.text: Face to show entertaining people

parts.note: pan = face (slang for the face; also to swing a camera round)

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn and play to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto (pantomime) is a British Christmas stage show for families, full of slapstick and audience participation.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: pantomime is the family stage show put on to amuse audiences at Christmas.

clue.text: In successful campaigns, American guided speeches?

indicators.note: In means the American-and-guided letters go inside the campaigns word

parts.note: military campaigns that succeed end in victories
to lead is to guide, so led means guided

explanation.surface: An American who steered winning election campaigns, ending with a question about speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that these speeches are a particular kind: farewells.
explanation.definitionFit: A valedictory is a farewell address, especially one given at a graduation, so these are speeches of a kind.

clue.text: Finished with good circular alternative to the Tube?

explanation.surface: Someone done with a nice circular route that avoids the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground; the London Overground is a separate rail network that often loops round the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling overground, on the surface, is the alternative to going by Tube.

clue.text: State delaying appearance of a commercial centre? It's true

definitions.note: the definition is a statement; the answer is the quality it asserts, truthfulness

indicators.note: the letter a is made to appear later, moving from the front of the state word to its end

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
the City is London's financial district, a commercial centre

explanation.surface: A claim about a postponed city development, followed by an assurance that it is true.
explanation.walkthrough: AVER with its first A delayed to the end becomes VERA. 'State' looks like a country or nation, but it is a verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracity is truthfulness, the quality of a statement that is accurate, so it is what saying something is so claims.

clue.text: Cheat's endless charm: ultimately evil demon, no saint

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of charm is cut off

parts.note: taken as written, before its last letter goes

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word evil

parts.note: taken as written, for its last letter

indicators.note: no means the saint letter is not wanted in the demon's name

explanation.surface: A warning that a cheat's charm hides evil, like a demon who is no saint.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR from charm without its end, L ending evil, and SATAN without S gives ATAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a fraud who claims skills he lacks, so he is a cheat or swindler.

clue.text: Quiet, internal part of Greater London

explanation.surface: A calm spot in the heart of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinner is a suburb in north-west London, in the borough of Harrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this suburb is one of the many districts making up Greater London.

clue.text: What may make Utes calm when roused?

definitions.text: What may make Utes calm when roused?

indicators.note: Roused means stirred up, so the letters are stirred.

explanation.surface: Asks what would pacify a Native American people once stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Utes are a Native American people of Utah; a calumet is the ceremonial peace pipe, so the whole clue defines while its middle is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumets, peace pipes, were smoked to make peace.

clue.text: Call on artist outwardly beaming?

parts.note: to dial = to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Phoning a painter who seems to be smiling on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaming' suggests a smile; here it means sending out beams, like spokes from a hub.
explanation.definitionFit: Radial means spreading outward from a centre, like rays.

clue.text: Gather information following action by reporter about lawyer

indicators.note: About means turned round.

explanation.surface: A journalist gathers facts from a lawyer after some legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About lawyer' wants to be a container round the lawyer; 'about' only turns ED round. A brief is British slang for a barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: To debrief is to question someone after a mission to gather what they learned.

clue.text: Turn handle and snatch a pole he has?

definitions.note: The definition is a description: he who has a pole.

explanation.surface: Someone twists a handle and grabs a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a door handle; it is slang for a name. A bargeman punts or steers with a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargeman works a barge and may push it along with a pole.

clue.text: Gossip — the very thing to support one information unit

indicators.note: In a down clue, a supporting piece goes underneath.

explanation.surface: Gossip is just the thing to prop up one's store of information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is ME, and in a down clue 'support' places GAB IT beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A megabit is a million bits of data.

clue.text: Professional model in good health

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model

explanation.surface: A professional model who is in fine health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good health' is the toast, not a condition. Prosit is the German drinking toast.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the German toast is said while raising a glass, wishing the drinkers good health.

clue.text: Seditious labourers being out of line finally sacked

indicators.note: sacked means plundered and ransacked, so the letters are wrecked and reassembled
out of means a letter is removed from being
finally picks the last letter of line

explanation.surface: Workers fired after stepping out of line are reported as dangerous agitators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes E (line's last letter, via 'finally') from BEING, giving BING; 'sacked' then shuffles LABOURERS plus BING.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabble-rousing speech stirs up a crowd against authority, so it is inflammatory and seditious.

clue.text: Use of mocking language is smooth? Yes, primarily

indicators.note: Primarily takes the first letter.

explanation.surface: Asks whether sarcasm is a smooth trick, and answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smooth' reads as an adjective about the mockery; it is the verb, to iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony is saying the opposite of what one means, often to mock.

clue.text: Armed struggle crosses Eastern river

explanation.surface: A war spills over onto the banks of an eastern river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham and Sunderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this is one of the rivers of north-east England.

clue.text: Type of Christian fighting group capturing area

indicators.note: The group captures A, holding it inside.

explanation.surface: A Christian militia seizing territory.
explanation.walkthrough: A Uniat belongs to an Eastern church that keeps its own rites but accepts the Pope's authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniat names a member of an Eastern Catholic church in union with Rome.

clue.text: Get large drink and suffer the consequences of it?

explanation.surface: Order a big drink and pay the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' pretends to mean fetch a drink; it means understand. The 'it' is the large drink, whose consequence is blurred vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing double is what too much drink does to you.

clue.text: Half dead court limiting enjoyment is no longer valid

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so half dead and the court abbreviation together go round the enjoyment
half of the word dead is kept, its front half

explanation.surface: A court curbing pleasure, half dead and no longer valid, like an obsolete ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limiting' acts on both pieces before it: half of dead and the court abbreviation together enclose the enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: A defunct law or body has ceased to exist or operate, so it no longer has any validity.

clue.text: Unscrupulous person reticent and mostly severe

indicators.note: 'mostly' cuts a letter off

explanation.surface: A crook who is quiet and rather stern.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition paints a rogue, while the wordplay describes someone shy and stern.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is a dishonest person, especially a lawyer.
